ceiling_directive: Add primitive quantitative interior-slack and target-perturbation richness conditions to the fixed-signature class, then prove that the explicit local-zeta rate is simultaneously achievable and minimax-sharp for risk and honest confidence length on that same class.
improvement_directive: Prove that the empirical extrapolation modulus at the pole-optimal cutoff satisfies \(\Omega_{G,\Sigma,k,s}(C_{G,\Sigma,k}^{\star})\lesssim R_{G,\Sigma,k}^{\star}\), and construct same-signature two-sided coefficient-mean perturbations yielding matching risk and honest-length lower bounds. Fully specify the Goldenshluger–Lepski selector and bias-aware interval, then establish uniform coverage and the corresponding upper rate.
critique: The note does not deliver the advertised matched minimax and honest-confidence-length frontier: thm:matched-frontier proves only an upper bound at the augmented quantity \(R^\dagger\) and a separate deterministic upper envelope \(R^\star\), with no comparison between them and no converse. The proposed geometry-selected cutoff is only an informal handle without a defined comparison statistic, threshold, or proved oracle inequality, so the feasible estimator has no explicit regular, critical, or irregular rate. The note also proves that its frozen class can have zero minimax risk and confidence length while \(R^\star>0\), demonstrating that the current assumptions cannot support the desired lower bounds. What is delivered is a nontrivial but specialized pseudo-inverse/local-zeta tail characterization and an augmented-modulus estimation upper bound on a certificate-defined reduced-form subclass, not a statistical frontier for the published model.
